stories.headline: Google Launches Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, Its Highest-Quality Real-Time Audio Model

key_facts.fact: Gemini 3.1 Flash Live is Google's highest-quality audio and speech model to date, optimized for low-latency real-time dialogue with native multimodal processing
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're advancing Gemini's real-time dialogue capabilities with Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, our highest-quality audio model

key_facts.fact: The model is available via the Gemini Live API in Google AI Studio for developers, and rolling out across Gemini Live app, Google Search Live, and Google Cloud for enterprises
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're launching Gemini 3.1 Flash Live via the Gemini Live API in Google AI Studio

key_facts.fact: The model uses thinkingLevel settings (minimal, low, medium, high) instead of thinkingBudget, with minimal as default for lowest latency
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini 3.1 uses thinkingLevel (with settings like minimal, low, medium, and high) instead of thinkingBudget. The default is minimal to optimize for lowest latency

key_facts.fact: Better filters background noise from traffic or television for improved task completion in noisy real-world environments, and better understands tone, emphasis, and intent
key_facts.excerpt: By better discerning relevant speech from environmental sounds like traffic or television, the model more effectively filters out background noise

key_facts.fact: Gemini Live with Flash Live now supports over 200 countries, and all audio output is watermarked to prevent misinformation
key_facts.excerpt: Everyone can experience it via Search Live and Gemini Live, which now supports over 200 countries

key_facts.fact: Input token limit of 131,072 and output token limit of 65,536; supports text, images, audio, and video inputs with text and audio outputs
key_facts.excerpt: Input token limit 131,072 Output token limit 65,536

stories.headline: Sakana AI's 'AI Scientist' Published in Nature, First Autonomous Research Tool to Pass Peer Review

key_facts.fact: The AI Scientist paper was published in Nature on March 26, 2026, describing a system that autonomously completes the entire machine learning research lifecycle
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are happy to announce that a paper describing all of this work and that includes new insights has been published in Nature

key_facts.fact: AI Scientist-v2 submitted an unedited, fully AI-generated paper to the ICLR 2025 ICBINB workshop, achieving an average score of 6.33 and scoring higher than 55% of human-authored papers
key_facts.excerpt: an average score of 6.33...surpassing the average human acceptance threshold and scoring higher than 55% of human-authored papers

key_facts.fact: The system autonomously generates research ideas, searches literature, designs and implements experiments using parallelized agentic tree search, and writes complete papers in LaTeX
key_facts.excerpt: autonomously generates research ideas, searches and reads literature, designs and implements experiments using parallelized agentic tree search, and writes complete papers in LaTeX

key_facts.fact: Scaling law results show quality of generated papers improves as underlying foundation models improve
key_facts.excerpt: As the underlying foundation models improve, the quality of the generated papers increases correspondingly

key_facts.fact: The automated reviewer achieved 69% balanced accuracy matching human reviewer performance, with F1-scores exceeding inter-human agreement from the NeurIPS 2021 consistency experiment
key_facts.excerpt: a balanced accuracy of 69% matching human reviewer performance, with F1-scores exceeding inter-human agreement from the NeurIPS 2021 consistency experiment

key_facts.fact: Collaboration between Sakana AI, University of British Columbia, Vector Institute, and University of Oxford, with Jeff Clune and Jakob Foerster as principal collaborators
key_facts.excerpt: researchers from UBC Computer Science, Sakana AI, the Vector Institute and the University of Oxford found a way to automate the entire research process

stories.headline: Apple Plans to Open Siri to Gemini, Claude, and Other Rival AI Services in iOS 27

key_facts.fact: Apple plans to open Siri to rival AI services beyond ChatGPT, allowing third-party AI apps to integrate directly with Siri via an Extensions system in iOS 27
key_facts.excerpt: Apple plans to open its Siri voice assistant to rival artificial intelligence services beyond its current partnership with ChatGPT, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday

key_facts.fact: Services like Google Gemini and Anthropic Claude would be able to integrate with Siri, with users choosing which AI service handles each request
key_facts.excerpt: would allow third-party AI apps to integrate directly with Siri, enabling users to route queries to services such as Alphabet's Gemini or Anthropic's Claude

key_facts.fact: Third-party AI apps downloaded from the App Store would work with Siri and other features under Apple Intelligence, ending ChatGPT's exclusive partnership status
key_facts.excerpt: third-party AI apps downloaded from the App Store, such as Google's Gemini or Anthropic's Claude, could be used to generate responses through Siri, similar to the existing ChatGPT integration

key_facts.fact: Apple could generate additional revenue by taking a share of subscriptions when users sign up for AI services through their devices
key_facts.excerpt: since some of these AIs need subscriptions, Apple could earn a cut when you sign up through your device

key_facts.fact: A first look at the Extensions feature is expected at Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference in June
key_facts.excerpt: Expect a first look at these features at the Worldwide Developers Conference in June

stories.headline: Google Launches Gemini Import Tool to Poach Users From ChatGPT and Claude

key_facts.fact: Google launched a memory import feature for Gemini that lets users transfer preferences, relationships, and personal context from other AI apps like ChatGPT and Claude
key_facts.excerpt: Google is adding a new memory import feature to Gemini, making it easier for customers to switch to Gemini AI from another AI service

key_facts.fact: Users can also import full chat history via ZIP file from ChatGPT and Claude, with support for searching and continuing past conversation threads in Gemini
key_facts.excerpt: users can now upload a ZIP file of their chat history from other AI providers. This allows them to search past conversation threads and continue building on them within Gemini

key_facts.fact: The import works by providing users a prompt to paste into their current AI app, which generates a preferences summary that can then be pasted into Gemini
key_facts.excerpt: The import option can be accessed through the Gemini settings, and it will provide a prompt to copy and paste into an existing AI app

key_facts.fact: Google is renaming its 'past chats' feature to 'memory' and the import is available to all personal Gemini users, excluding EEA, Switzerland, and the UK
key_facts.excerpt: Google announced the rollout of simple switching tools that work with other AI apps for all personal Gemini users

key_facts.fact: The move comes weeks after Anthropic made switching to Claude easier, intensifying platform competition among AI chatbots
key_facts.excerpt: Just weeks after Anthropic made switching to Claude AI easier, Google has followed suit to make switching to Gemini easier

stories.headline: OpenAI's ChatGPT Ad Pilot Tops $100M ARR in Under Two Months

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's ad business surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue less than two months after launching its US pilot
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's nascent ads business has surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue less than two months after launching its pilot in the U.S.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is working with more than 600 advertisers and reports no impact on privacy-related trust metrics
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is working with more than 600 advertisers and has seen no impact on privacy-related trust metrics

key_facts.fact: Roughly 85% of OpenAI's free and Go users in the US are eligible to see ads, but less than 20% are shown them on a daily basis
key_facts.excerpt: Roughly 85% of OpenAI's free and Go users in the U.S. are eligible to see ads, but less than 20% are shown them on a daily basis

key_facts.fact: Ads appear at the bottom of ChatGPT's answers, do not influence responses, and are clearly labeled; users under 18 don't see ads
key_facts.excerpt: Ads within ChatGPT will appear at the bottom of the chatbot's answers, will not influence its responses and will be clearly labeled

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is exploring expansion to Canada, Australia, and New Zealand; the ad push was ridiculed by rival Anthropic in its first Super Bowl campaign
key_facts.excerpt: The company is also beginning to explore additional testing in Canada, Australia and New Zealand

stories.headline: OpenAI Indefinitely Pauses ChatGPT Adult Mode, Consolidates Around Coding and AGI

key_facts.fact: OpenAI has indefinitely paused development of an erotic 'adult mode' for ChatGPT, which CEO Sam Altman had first floated in October
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has put the kibosh on yet another project — at least for the time being. On Thursday, the Financial Times reported that the AI company would be 'indefinitely' pausing plans to develop an 'erotic' mode for ChatGPT

key_facts.fact: The adult mode faced pushback over encouraging unhealthy attachments and potential exposure of minors; one adviser warned OpenAI could be building a 'sexy suicide coach'
key_facts.excerpt: the sexual chatbot faced growing pushback over how it could encourage unhealthy attachments to AI systems and expose minors to problematic sexual content

key_facts.fact: The pause follows OpenAI's discontinuation of Sora video generation on March 24 and deprioritization of Instant Checkout e-commerce feature
key_facts.excerpt: Adult mode is only the latest side quest that OpenAI has abandoned over the past week as the AI giant consolidates its focus

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's current priority is the development of a 'superapp' combining ChatGPT, Codex coding agent, and Atlas web browser
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's current priority is the development of a 'superapp' that combines ChatGPT, its Codex coding agent, and its Atlas web browser

key_facts.fact: The Sora discontinuation ended a $1 billion deal with Disney that had never closed; the Sora research team is redirecting to world simulation for robotics
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI announced the move publicly on Tuesday... the Sora research team continues to focus on world simulation research to advance robotics

key_facts.excerpt: Zendesk today announced the completion of its acquisition of Forethought, an AI agent platform enabling Zendesk to immediately offer self-improving AI agents

key_facts.fact: Forethought AI Agents work seamlessly within Zendesk and across any platform, designed so every interaction makes the system smarter and every outcome is measurable

key_facts.fact: Zendesk CEO Tom Eggemeier positioned the acquisition as moving beyond conversation management to AI that drives real outcomes, calling it the 'agentic service era'
key_facts.excerpt: We are moving beyond systems that manage conversations to AI that drives real outcomes. No one but Zendesk is delivering self-improving AI agents like ours

stories.headline: Federal Judge Grants Anthropic Preliminary Injunction Against Pentagon Supply Chain Ban

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Rita Lin granted Anthropic a preliminary injunction blocking the Pentagon's supply chain risk designation and a presidential directive ordering federal agencies to stop using Anthropic's technology
key_facts.excerpt: A federal judge in California has indefinitely blocked the Pentagon's effort to 'punish' Anthropic by labeling it a supply chain risk

key_facts.fact: The 43-page ruling called the designation 'Orwellian' and found it constituted 'classic illegal First Amendment retaliation' for Anthropic's public criticism of government AI policy
key_facts.excerpt: Punishing Anthropic for bringing public scrutiny to the government's contracting position is classic illegal First Amendment retaliation

key_facts.fact: Judge Lin stayed implementation of her ruling for one week to allow the government to appeal, and the supply chain designation cannot take effect while the injunction is in place
key_facts.excerpt: Lin also stayed the effective date of the supply-chain designation, meaning that it cannot take place while the injunction is in place

key_facts.fact: The ruling found the supply chain risk designation is usually reserved for foreign intelligence agencies and terrorists, not American companies
key_facts.excerpt: Lin wrote that the supply chain risk designation is usually reserved for foreign intelligence agencies and terrorists, not for American companies

key_facts.fact: The judge wrote that Anthropic showed it was suffering irreparable harm and that the broad measures appeared designed to punish the company rather than address national security
key_facts.excerpt: these broad measures do not appear to be directed at the government's stated national security interests... these measures appear designed to punish Anthropic
